name: collapse-recovery
description: Chapter 7: Drive an employee's need gauges to genuine collapse purely through unrelieved neglect. #680's rest fix (resting drains at 0, not idle rate) closed the pathway this file used to rely on: a fully idle employee, even with zero reachable living_quarters anywhere on the map, is auto-routed by autoInsertNeedTasks into a self-targeted, zero-distance ground-rest the SAME tick their gauge first dips under its warning threshold, which now holds flat (0 drain) for the rest's whole duration and tops back up — direct probing (GameLoop.ts, tickNeedGauges/autoInsertNeedTasks) confirmed a purely-idle employee stabilizes in a permanent warning-threshold oscillation and cannot reach the collapse floor at any tick budget tested, with or without a living_quarters on the map. Genuine neglect that still bites (per #680's own acceptance framing, 'a site that genuinely neglects its crew still revolts — the mechanism keeps its teeth', its individual-collapse equivalent) instead requires the employee kept continuously BUSY with no living_quarters ever built: while activeActionId is set, autoInsertNeedTasks only queues a rest unclaimed (never self-claims a busy employee), so drain proceeds at the faster 'working' rate uninterrupted by any rest until tickCollapse's own unconditional threshold check fires — confirmed for real via a direct probe (`employee dispatch <id> x:<own x> z:<own z>` twice, matching the pattern #680's own needs.integration.test.ts CONTRAST acceptance case uses to prove the punishing mechanism survives the fix) and re-derived from that run below, not assumed from the file's old, now-false claim. #1062 moved NEED_HARD_THRESHOLDS.fatigue from 5 to 0 and added rest-priority ordering (a queued rest always wins the claim race against any other targeted action for the same employee, EmployeeDispatchSteps.ts) plus #945's mid-execution defer (autoInsertNeedTasks never even queues a rest while the employee is still executing a claimed task). Together these make the file's OLD second-collapse technique (redispatch once per fixed tick batch) permanently unable to reproduce a second collapse: the instant any task completes with fatigue already under NEED_SOFT_THRESHOLDS.fatigue (25), a proactive rest is queued AND immediately promoted ahead of anything already staged in taskQueue, however many redispatches were queued in advance or however tightly they're issued — direct-probed exhaustively (every redispatch cadence from once-per-25-ticks down to once-per-tick, and pre-staging up to MAX_EMPLOYEE_TASK_QUEUE_DEPTH redispatches at once) and confirmed genuine, intended #1062 behavior rather than a bug: the needs system now reliably protects an employee from being redirected back to work ahead of a rest it already queued for them. The only way left to force a genuine SECOND collapse is the inverse of that same protection: dispatch while fatigue is ALREADY below NEED_THRESHOLDS.fatigue.low (40, productivity.ts's duration formula) but still at/above the soft threshold (25) — computeTaskDuration's needMultiplier then stretches the single dispatched task's own fixed duration (ceil(BASE_TASK_DURATION_TICKS / 0.75) = 27 ticks) far enough past the ~2.4/tick working drain (working rate 2, ×1.20 low-morale multiplier post-first-collapse) to run fatigue through 0 while STILL mid-execution — #945's own guard then keeps a rest from ever being queued during that whole span, and tickCollapse's unconditional check (which runs before that same tick's task-completion pass) catches it before the task ever finishes naturally. Re-derived live: after the first collapse-rest caps fatigue at NEED_REST_NO_BUILDING_CAP (70), 60 further IDLE ticks (no redispatch) drain it via the idle rate down to ~42 — still safely above the soft threshold the whole time, so no rest is ever queued — then one redispatch there reliably collapses a second time at absolute tick 129 (cumulative tick ~129, well inside the 25-tick batch that follows).

expect.note: baseline before the forced-work run below — fresh hire's needs start full. No living_quarters is ever built in this file (deliberate, real neglect) — this driller (seed 42, dusty_hollow, spawns at (82,34)) has no rest destination anywhere on the map.

steps.description: Left unmarked with role bootstrap like needs-collapse-visual's equivalent dispatch: no console command a player would reach for creates a targeted work order at an employee's own position — this exists purely to keep the driller genuinely, continuously busy (working-rate drain, no idle window autoInsertNeedTasks could route a self-rest into) so neglect is real instead of accidental.

expect.note: 25 ticks of continuous forced work (working-rate drain) is not yet enough to collapse a fresh hire — real, verified via a direct engine probe

steps.description: Second dispatch keeps the driller continuously working across the first task's completion, the same handoff needs-collapse-visual's own second Walt dispatch documents — a redispatch issued while still busy is harmless (queues behind the active task) and this one lands right around the first task's own completion, so no idle tick opens up for autoInsertNeedTasks to route a saving rest into before the gauge crosses its collapse floor.

expect.note: cumulative tick 50: genuine collapse via continuous unrelieved forced work, no living_quarters anywhere on the map — re-derived from a real run, not assumed. wellBeing is NOT asserted decreased here: the same batch that drives the collapse also runs the collapse-rest that immediately follows it (no building involved, so it tops gauges back up per NEED_REST_NO_BUILDING_CAP), and a real run shows wellBeing net INCREASE across this step (58.15 → 62.37) even though the employee is flagged COLLAPSING at the end of it — the gauge recovery outweighs the morale hit within this one batch.

steps.note: cumulative tick 110 — deliberately NOT redispatched this time (#1062 finding, see the file's own description): the collapse-rest above completes on its own and tops fatigue out at NEED_REST_NO_BUILDING_CAP (70), then 60 further idle ticks drain it via the idle rate down to ~42 — still safely above NEED_SOFT_THRESHOLDS.fatigue (25) the whole time, so no proactive rest is ever queued to race the next dispatch below. minFatigue increases net across this whole step (0 at the start, still mid-collapse-rest, to ~41.8 by the end) even though the back half of the step is pure idle drain — the rest's own recovery dominates. collapsedCount is a live snapshot of currently-collapsing employees, not a running total — by cumulative tick 110 the first collapse's rest has long since completed (~tick67), so it correctly reads 0 again here, not 1. Real run: fatigue 0 -> 70 (rest completes ~tick67) -> ~41.8 (idle drain to tick110).

steps.description: Dispatched now, at fatigue ~42 — already below NEED_THRESHOLDS.fatigue.low (40), so computeTaskDuration's needMultiplier stretches this single task's own fixed duration (ceil(20 / 0.75) = 27 ticks) far enough past the ~2.4/tick working drain that fatigue runs through 0 while still mid-execution. #945's mid-execution guard keeps a rest from ever being queued during that span (unlike a task claimed at full fatigue, which completes normally before ever nearing the floor), so tickCollapse's own unconditional check is what interrupts it below, not a natural completion.

expect.note: cumulative tick 135: neglect is not a one-off — a single task dispatched into the low-fatigue productivity band runs long enough to collapse this employee again (real run: fires at absolute tick 129, well inside this batch). wellBeing is asserted flat at 0 rather than decreased — morale was already floored by the first collapse (NEED_MORALE_EFFECT_PENALTIES' repeated 'critical' penalty and clampScore's own 0 floor) and stays there; there is no further room for this second collapse to push it down.
